dedupe_keys.name: joan human automated driving experiment framework

description: JOAN is a framework for human-in-the-loop experiments with automated vehicles in the CARLA driving simulator. Its interface links CARLA scenes to a person using virtual reality, steering or other input devices, with support for haptic feedback and stored experiment settings. A researcher can define and repeat interaction scenarios without writing all of the simulator integration code. The road layout, simulated traffic duration and geographical setting depend on the CARLA world and experiment chosen; JOAN has no fixed observed road dataset. Its GitHub source and documentation are public, and the repository LICENSE file contains GPL version 3 despite the API classifier returning NOASSERTION. The software can help test how human drivers respond to automated vehicles and supply behavioural assumptions for traffic simulations. It relies on CARLA and compatible hardware, so no experiment result can be inferred from source availability alone. Simulated human responses may not transfer directly to real road conditions. No separate catalogue record or first-review draft was found for JOAN. The code was not installed and no participant experiment was performed. A caveat is that hardware and CARLA versions may affect whether an example can be repeated. No directly related catalogue record was established.
